suread: review R1 素读（只读 text/，未开 md）

facts.fact: 接下来一周农场工作吞掉了她
facts.anchor: my work at the farm consumed me

facts.fact: 在 Greer House 之外她尽量不待在屋里；屋里除了 Gazzie 是空的
facts.anchor: which was empty, besides Gazzie

facts.fact: Virginia 姨妈越发频繁地外出访 Henri、办神秘的事
facts.anchor: Aunt Virginia left to visit Henri and run mysterious errands more and more frequently

facts.fact: 她发现温室与院子没有异象异响，与原楼不同
facts.anchor: the conservatory and yard were free from odd sights and sounds, unlike the original building

facts.fact: 她在露台上吃饭画画
facts.anchor: I’d eat and sketch on the patio

facts.fact: 日落后速战速决洗澡、吃褪黑素、戴廉价眼罩、塞耳机
facts.anchor: shower quickly, pop melatonin tablets, slip on a dollar-store eye mask, and shove headphones over my ears

facts.fact: 她拒绝看见或听见任何异常
facts.anchor: I refused to see or hear anything out of the ordinary

facts.fact: 黑影掠过门口她解释成光线错觉
facts.anchor: I told myself it was a fluke of the light

facts.fact: 任何咕哝都被解释成老维多利亚房的声学
facts.anchor: any muttering was old Victorian acoustics

facts.fact: 她答应自己以后再去开 Leon 的锁箱、继续查 Mama 出走
facts.anchor: I promised myself I’d open Uncle Leon’s lockbox and continue my search for answers to Mama’s escape

facts.fact: 不敢惹 Gazzie 生气：她可能把剥皮岗撤掉
facts.anchor: I couldn’t risk angering Gazzie; she might pull me from skinning duty

facts.fact: 剥皮是她目前最喜欢的活，她猜也是讨 Gazzie 欢心的钥匙
facts.anchor: my favorite task yet and, I suspected, the key to impressing her

facts.fact: 剥皮落进节奏
facts.anchor: Skinning itself fell into a rhythm

facts.fact: 剥得越多她越喜欢手感：腹部肉的软、绿色骨板滑过指头
facts.anchor: the softness of belly flesh, the slickness of green plates coasting along my fingers

facts.fact: 周中她说服 Harrison 不再需要监督
facts.anchor: Halfway through the week, I convinced Harrison I didn’t need supervision

facts.fact: 她不想让他看见她的手在鳄鱼皮上流连
facts.anchor: I didn’t want him to see the way my hands lingered over the alligators’ skin

facts.fact: 第一次剥皮整整一周后她太入神忘了午饭
facts.anchor: A full week after my first skinning, I was so engrossed I forgot about lunch

facts.fact: 她从地上捡起一块肉时视野收窄
facts.anchor: I picked up a chunk of flesh from the floor and my vision tunneled

facts.fact: 她甩开手、撑在桌上等视力回来
facts.anchor: Throwing out my hand, I leaned heavily on the table, waiting for my sight to return

facts.fact: 视力恢复时墙钟指着下午三点
facts.anchor: the wall clock read three in the afternoon

facts.fact: 难怪发虚
facts.anchor: No wonder I felt faint

facts.fact: 一进前办公室就意识到水壶落下了，但太饿不想回去
facts.anchor: I’d left my water bottle behind, but I was too hungry to go back

facts.fact: 她决定午饭后再接水
facts.anchor: I’d fill it up after lunch

facts.fact: Nova 被她的低声咒骂惊得抬头、把手机放到桌上
facts.anchor: Nova’s head jerked up at my whispered curse, and she set her phone on her desk

facts.fact: Nova 皱眉问：看见 Joe 了吗
facts.anchor: Have you seen Joe?” she asked, eyebrows furrowed

facts.fact: 她脑雾中艰难回想
facts.anchor: I struggled to think through my brain fog

facts.fact: 那一周她开始注意到 Joe 的几件事
facts.anchor: That week, I’d begun to notice certain things about Joe

facts.fact: 他在走廊里离她近得无礼、擦肩时撞她肩膀
facts.anchor: He walked disrespectfully close in hallways, bumping my shoulder when we passed

facts.fact: 他休息时躺在皮卡后斗里、用一把阴森的黑柄厨刀切橙子
facts.anchor: He lounged in the bed of his pickup truck on breaks, slicing oranges with a sinister, black-handled kitchen knife

facts.fact: 每次对上眼他都咧嘴，像掌握了什么优势
facts.anchor: Every time our eyes met, he smirked, like he knew something that gave him the upper hand

facts.fact: 他的存在通常给整个公司蒙上一层黏腻的膜
facts.anchor: His presence usually cast a slimy film over Greer Fine Alligators

facts.fact: 但一整天她没有感到那种爬行般的不适
facts.anchor: but I hadn’t felt that creeping sensation all day

facts.fact: 她答：没见过他
facts.anchor: Haven’t seen him,” I replied

facts.fact: Nova 叹气拿起手机，她继续走向休息室
facts.anchor: Nova sighed, picking up her phone, and I continued to the break room

facts.fact: Harrison 靠在台边往咖啡里倒半奶
facts.anchor: Harrison leaned against the counter, stirring half-and-half into a cup of coffee

facts.fact: 他看见她点点头、退出房间、敲着手机
facts.anchor: he nodded then left the room, tapping on his phone

facts.fact: 她松了口气，坐到午餐桌边吃沙拉
facts.anchor: Relieved, I slid into a seat at the lunch table and took a bite of my salad

facts.fact: 不到十分钟 Harrison 回来，又倒一杯咖啡坐到她对面
facts.anchor: Less than ten minutes later, Harrison returned, filled another coffee cup, and sat across from me

facts.fact: 她内心呻吟、勉强堆出一个温吞的笑
facts.anchor: Groaning inwardly, I plastered on a lukewarm smile

facts.fact: 两人闲聊，他顺口提到父亲
facts.anchor: We made small talk until he mentioned his father in passing

facts.fact: 她想起 Greer House 他书里那张照片
facts.anchor: I remembered the photo in his book at Greer House

facts.fact: 她不假思索问：你们亲近吗
facts.anchor: Without thinking, I asked, “Are you close?

facts.fact: 他快速眨眼、从杯子上抬起头：我们曾经
facts.anchor: Blinking rapidly, he looked up from his cup. “We were.

facts.fact: 她自问：那是父亲死了还是闹翻了
facts.anchor: Did that mean his father was dead or estranged?

facts.fact: 她脸颊发烫、后悔没安静吃沙拉
facts.anchor: My cheeks warmed. I should have eaten my salad in silence

facts.fact: 她半句道歉：我不是那个意思——
facts.anchor: I didn’t mean—

facts.fact: 他说父亲已死一段时间了
facts.anchor: It’s been a while since he died

facts.fact: 两人住处相隔十分钟车程
facts.anchor: We lived ten minutes from one another

facts.fact: 每周日一起钓鱼，直到他生病
facts.anchor: Fished every Sunday until he got sick

facts.fact: 父亲没有医保；雇主是真心黑的混蛋
facts.anchor: He didn’t have health insurance, employers were real assholes—

facts.fact: 他把她打量一遍，像自己说漏了什么
facts.anchor: He gave me a once-over, like he’d slipped up

facts.fact: 她问：怎么了
facts.anchor: “What?” I asked.

facts.fact: 他含糊：这个嘛……你知道的
facts.anchor: Well, it’s…you know.

facts.fact: 她追：知道什么
facts.anchor: Know what?

facts.fact: 他点破：医保那件事
facts.anchor: Blinking, he said, “The health insurance thing.

facts.fact: 她说自己完全不明白他在说什么
facts.anchor: I have no idea what you’re talking about

facts.fact: 他说 Greer Fine Alligators 也不提供医保
facts.anchor: Greer Fine Alligators doesn’t offer health insurance either

facts.fact: 她脸颊像着了火
facts.anchor: My cheeks felt like they were on fire

facts.fact: 医保是她找工作的第一考量
facts.anchor: Insurance was the first thing I looked for in a job

facts.fact: POTS 至今没花她太多钱，但恶化或添新症状就需要
facts.anchor: POTS hadn’t cost me too much yet, but if it worsened or other symptoms cropped up, I’d need it

facts.fact: 只有最残忍最贪婪的公司才不给员工上保险
facts.anchor: Only the cruelest, greediest companies didn’t cover employees

facts.fact: 她质疑：一个暴力事故随时可能发生的鳄鱼农场怎么敢不上
facts.anchor: How could an alligator farm, where violent accidents were a real possibility, not offer it?

facts.fact: 她震惊 Gazzie 还能在员工面前昂首
facts.anchor: I was shocked Gazzie could hold her head high among her employees

facts.fact: 她自陈不确定现在还能与员工对视
facts.anchor: I wasn’t sure I’d be able to look them in the eye now

facts.fact: 她问：你跟 Gazzie 谈过这事吗
facts.anchor: Have you talked to Gazzie about it?

facts.fact: 他干笑一声：她是坚定的不，会侵蚀利润
facts.anchor: With a mirthless laugh, he said, “She’s a solid no. Cuts into profits.

facts.fact: 她说：也许我可以试试，以后
facts.anchor: I can give it a try. Eventually.

facts.fact: 他笑了但笑意没到眼睛
facts.anchor: He smiled, but it didn’t reach his eyes

facts.fact: 叙述者补一句：两人都知道她不会听
facts.anchor: We both knew she wouldn’t listen

facts.fact: 沉默后他反问：你和你妈妈亲近吗
facts.anchor: Were you and your mom close?

facts.fact: 她不知如何作答
facts.anchor: I wasn’t sure how to answer

facts.fact: 「是」的那一面：除工作与学校外她是她唯一说话的人
facts.anchor: Yes, in that she was the only person I spoke to outside work and school

facts.fact: 「否」的那一面：她们不断争吵、她拒绝按她的样子看她
facts.anchor: No, in that we argued constantly, and she refused to see me the way I saw myself

facts.fact: 她自问：怎么会跟一个认定自己是怪物的女人亲近
facts.anchor: How could I be close with a woman who thought I was a monster?

facts.fact: 她决定给中性答案
facts.anchor: I’d go with a neutral answer

facts.fact: 她答：我和她住在一起直到她去世
facts.anchor: I lived with her until she died

facts.fact: 他评价：那很暖心
facts.anchor: “That’s sweet.

facts.fact: 她差点笑出来但忍住了
facts.anchor: I almost laughed but held back

facts.fact: 她不能坦白自己照顾她并非全出于女儿之爱
facts.anchor: I couldn’t reveal that I didn’t care for her entirely out of daughterly love

facts.fact: 也不能坦白：她让她相信她是唯一的选择
facts.anchor: that she’d made me believe she was my only option

facts.fact: 她绕开真相：她有红斑狼疮、需要大量照料
facts.anchor: She had lupus, so she needed a lot of help

facts.fact: 肾移植失败，所以——
facts.anchor: Then she had a kidney transplant that didn’t go well, so.

facts.fact: 她说不能讲她死的那晚
facts.anchor: I couldn’t get into the night she died

facts.fact: 他声音变软、卸下客气的表层
facts.anchor: His voice gentled, dropping the polite veneer

facts.fact: 他说：听起来像是牺牲
facts.anchor: Sounds like a sacrifice.

facts.fact: 她对他的同情感到意外、端详他
facts.anchor: Surprised at his sympathy, I regarded him as he gazed into his cup

facts.fact: 她疑心他在装朋友：这是又一种策略
facts.anchor: Was he trying to act like my friend now? This was another tactic.

facts.fact: 她连读成：又一次试图卸她的防、削弱她
facts.anchor: Another attempt to disarm me. Weaken me.

facts.fact: 她强作欢快：也不算。不知道没有她我会在哪
facts.anchor: I forced a cheerful tone. “Not really. I don’t know where I’d be without her.

facts.fact: 她自注：那是全部真相
facts.anchor: That was the whole truth.

facts.fact: 又一阵沉默后她咕哝了个借口冲出休息室
facts.anchor: I mumbled an excuse and rushed out of the break room

facts.fact: 她说自己宁可和死鳄鱼待着也不重述过去
facts.anchor: I’d much rather spend my time with dead alligators than relive the past

facts.fact: 走廊半途听见 Harrison 喊她名字
facts.anchor: Halfway down the hallway, I heard Harrison calling my name

facts.fact: 他喊的是 Dart、小跑过来、微微喘
facts.anchor: “Dart,” he repeated, slightly out of breath as he jogged toward me

facts.fact: 他转述：Gazzie 要她俩过一遍文件的进度
facts.anchor: I forgot. Gazzie wants you and me to go over the progress you’ve made on the files.

facts.fact: 她问为什么、不想回那间潮湿逼仄的屋子
facts.anchor: I didn’t want to return to that dank, cramped room

facts.fact: 她剥皮正上手：每一次更精准、划痕更少
facts.anchor: I was on a roll with skinning, each attempt more precise, with fewer nicks

facts.fact: 他猜：她在考虑再雇人帮忙
facts.anchor: I think she’s considering hiring someone else to help

facts.fact: 她宽慰：至少是临时调岗
facts.anchor: At least it was a temporary reassignment

facts.fact: 她请求改到明天、指了指自己的牛仔裤
facts.anchor: Can we do it tomorrow? I’m already kind of—” I gestured to my jeans

facts.fact: 她围裙戴了但还是有肉屑滑落到小腿、留下深色污渍
facts.anchor: some flesh had slipped out of my hands and landed on my lower legs, leaving a dark stain

facts.fact: 他说：看来你要成为「 messy 那一类」了
facts.anchor: I see you’re going to be one of the messy ones

facts.fact: 她比划呕吐问要不要垃圾桶、立刻觉得自己幼稚
facts.anchor: “Need a trash can?” I mimed vomiting, then immediately felt childish

facts.fact: 他黑着脸：真好笑。也许你可以先收拾
facts.anchor: Scowling, he said, “Very funny. Maybe you can clean up before we get started.

facts.fact: 她问：她现在就要我们？
facts.anchor: She needs us this minute?

facts.fact: 他耸肩：她过会儿想试试剥皮间
facts.anchor: She wants to take a crack at the skinning room in a little bit

facts.fact: 他说自己也不明白急在哪
facts.anchor: I’m not sure what the rush is about

facts.fact: 消息是 Joe 传来的
facts.anchor: Word came from Joe

facts.fact: 他猜她又在闹脾气
facts.anchor: She’s probably in a mood

facts.fact: 她说 Joe 根本不在
facts.anchor: Joe’s not even around

facts.fact: 他说三十来分钟前 Joe 留了张便条给他
facts.anchor: He left me a note thirty or so minutes ago

facts.fact: 她瞪他、认定有可疑
facts.anchor: Something suspicious was going on

facts.fact: 疑点一：为何让 Joe 转告而不自己发短信
facts.anchor: Why would Gazzie have Joe tell Harrison instead of texting Harrison herself?

facts.fact: 她自解：也许她正好在合适的时机撞上 Joe
facts.anchor: Maybe she’d just run into Joe at the opportune moment

facts.fact: 疑点二：Joe 为何留条不当面说
facts.anchor: why had Joe left a note for Harrison instead of telling him face-to-face?

facts.fact: 疑点三：Harrison 既然知道，为何还让她悠闲吃完午饭才说
facts.anchor: why had he let me take a leisurely lunch break before saying so?

facts.fact: 疑点四：他真会忘吗
facts.anchor: Would he really have forgotten?

facts.fact: 她自答：他第二杯下午茶还没喝
facts.anchor: I supposed he hadn’t had that second cup of afternoon coffee yet

facts.fact: 她补一句：他终究不是完美的员工
facts.anchor: He wasn’t a perfect employee, after all

facts.fact: 她闷闷地说去拿水壶
facts.anchor: Sullenly, I said, “I’ll just grab my water bottle.

facts.fact: 他说休息室也有水
facts.anchor: You know we have water in the break room, right?

facts.fact: 她说 prefer 自己的杯子
facts.anchor: “I like mine.

facts.fact: 她没力气解释电解质水、继而要交代病史
facts.anchor: I didn’t have the energy to mention my electrolyte water, which would lead to explaining my medical history

facts.fact: 她预判他必会说她其实不需要喝那么多
facts.anchor: when he inevitably told me I didn’t actually need to drink so much of it

facts.fact: 他自告奋勇去取
facts.anchor: I’ll get it for you, then

facts.fact: 她内心：往里下鼠药吗？今天不行
facts.anchor: And put rat poison in it? Not today.

facts.fact: 她答：我还行，谢谢
facts.anchor: I’m quite capable, thanks

facts.fact: 他抹了抹沙色头发：你一直这么难搞吗
facts.anchor: He ran a hand through his sandy hair. “Have you always been such a pain?

facts.fact: 她回嘴：你能激发出我最好的一面
facts.anchor: You bring out the best in me,

facts.fact: 她走开时尽量体面——牛仔裤上糊着鳄鱼血
facts.anchor: walking away in as dignified a manner as I could with alligator blood smeared across my jeans

facts.fact: 某些方面她高兴两人回到公开的互相讨厌
facts.anchor: I was happy we were back to our open dislike of each other

facts.fact: 她承认紧绷的对话变得有点好玩
facts.anchor: Our taut conversations had become kind of fun

facts.fact: 且比真诚更让她舒服
facts.anchor: and were a lot more comfortable than sincerity

facts.fact: 剥皮间门外她停住：屋里是黑的
facts.anchor: Outside the skinning room, I paused. The room was dark.

facts.fact: 她不记得自己关了灯、猜有别的员工进来过
facts.anchor: I didn’t remember turning off the lights, but maybe another employee had come in behind me

facts.fact: 推门后空气湿热得像到了户外
facts.anchor: I found the air humid and hot, like I’d stepped outside

facts.fact: 持续一滴一滴的回响在空旷空间里
facts.anchor: A persistent drip echoed in the cavernous space

facts.fact: 漏水又冒出来了
facts.anchor: The leak had sprung again.

facts.fact: 身前某处响起一声嘶
facts.anchor: A hiss sounded somewhere in front of me.

facts.fact: 脚不听使唤，像陷在泥里
facts.anchor: as though they were stuck in mud

facts.fact: 她逐条过可能性：管子松阀？去皮用的水枪？
facts.anchor: I cycled through all the possibilities: Maybe it was a loose valve to some pipe? The pressure washer for fleshing skins?

facts.fact: 她屏住呼吸走进去摸开关
facts.anchor: Holding my breath, I stepped fully inside the room and felt for the switch

facts.fact: 灯立刻亮起、照亮整间屋
facts.anchor: The lights blinked on immediately, illuminating the room

facts.fact: 一条活的鳄鱼七到八英尺，躺在剥皮桌脚边、嘴大张
facts.anchor: A live alligator, seven or eight feet long, lay by the foot of the skinning table, its mouth open wide

facts.fact: 几十颗牙围着张开的鲑红色口腔，滴着唾液
facts.anchor: Dozens of teeth outlined a gaping, salmon-colored maw dripping with saliva

facts.fact: 湿而肥的舌头平摊在口腔底部
facts.anchor: A wet, fat tongue lay flat along the bottom of its mouth

facts.fact: 它又嘶了一声，声音大、空、可怕
facts.anchor: It hissed again, the sound loud and hollow and terrible

facts.fact: 她僵住、想怎么吓退鳄鱼：像对付熊那样张开双臂冲上去？装死？
facts.anchor: How did you scare off an alligator? Did you run at it with your arms open, like with a bear? Did you play dead?

facts.fact: 她当即否定装死
facts.anchor: Definitely not the latter.

facts.fact: 她纳闷这怎么不在培训里
facts.anchor: How had this not been part of my training?

facts.fact: 另一个担忧：吃了午饭但没喝水、而且很热
facts.anchor: I’d eaten lunch, but I hadn’t had water, and I was hot. Very hot.

facts.fact: 转身要跑时房间跟着她转
facts.anchor: As I turned to run, the room turned with me

facts.fact: 她感觉鳄鱼在动、也许扑过来了
facts.anchor: I sensed the alligator moving—lunging, maybe

facts.fact: 她已经向前栽出、从她留了缝的门出去
facts.anchor: I was already falling forward, out the door I’d left cracked open

facts.fact: 她在走廊里踉跄约六步、脚被什么绊住摔倒
facts.anchor: I stumbled about six steps down the hallway before my foot caught on something, throwing me to the floor

facts.fact: 视野发灰；以为听见喊声但不确定
facts.anchor: My vision grayed. I thought I heard shouting but couldn’t be sure.

facts.fact: 不知何时她睁开没压在混凝土上的那只眼
facts.anchor: I opened the eye not pressed into the concrete floor

facts.fact: 在剥皮间的门槛上，Gazzie 压在鳄鱼身上
facts.anchor: On the skinning room’s threshold, Gazzie lay on top of the alligator

facts.fact: 她徒手合住鳄鱼的上下颚
facts.anchor: holding its jaws closed with her bare hands

facts.fact: 她的嘴张着，像在尖叫
facts.anchor: her mouth open in a scream
